Tafsir of Surah Fussilat

It is a Meccan surah.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Ha Mim. A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.﴾ That is: the Qur'an is sent down from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, like His saying: ﴿Say, "The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord in truth"﴾ [al-Nahl: 102], and His saying: ﴿And indeed, it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. The trustworthy Spirit has brought it down upon your heart, that you may be among the warners﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 192-194].

* *

His saying: ﴿A Book whose verses have been detailed﴾ means: its meanings have been made clear and its rulings have been firmly established. ﴿An Arabic Qur'an﴾ means: it is in an Arabic language, clear and evident. Its meanings are distinguished and its words are plain, not obscure. Like His saying: ﴿A Book whose verses have been perfected and then detailed from One who is All-Wise and Acquainted [with all things]﴾ [Hud: 1]. That is: it is miraculous in both its wording and its meaning. ﴿Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or behind it. It is a revelation from One who is All-Wise and Praiseworthy﴾ [Fussilat: 42].

* *

His saying: ﴿for a people who know﴾ means: only the firmly grounded scholars recognize this clarity and explicitness. ﴿As a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾ means: at times it gives good tidings to the believers, and at times it warns the disbelievers. ﴿But most of them turn away, so they do not hear﴾ means: most of the Quraysh, so they do not understand anything from it despite its clarity and explicitness.

﴿And they say, "Our hearts are in coverings﴾ meaning: in sealed wrappings ﴿against that to which you invite us, and in our ears is deafness﴾ meaning: deafness to what you have brought us, ﴿and between us and you is a screen﴾ so nothing of what you say reaches us. ﴿So work, for indeed we are working﴾ meaning: you work according to your way, and we work according to our way; we will not follow you.

The eminent Imam 'Abd ibn Humayd said in his Musnad: Ibn Abi Shaybah related to me: 'Ali ibn Mushir related to us from al-Ajlah, from al-Dhayyal ibn Harmalah al-Asadi, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Quraysh gathered one day and said: "Look for the most knowledgeable among you in magic, soothsaying and poetry. Let him go to this man who has divided our community, scattered our affair, and reviled our religion, and let him speak to him, and we will see what he replies." They said: "We know of no one but 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah." They said: "You, O Abu al-Walid." So 'Utbah came to him and said: "O Muhammad, are you better, or 'Abd Allah?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained silent. He said: "Are you better, or 'Abd al-Muttalib?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained silent. He said: "If you claim that these people are better than you, then they worshipped the gods you have reviled. And if you claim that you are better than them, then speak, so that we may hear your words. By Allah, we have never seen a young man more ill-omened for his people than you: you have divided our community, scattered our affair, reviled our religion, and disgraced us among the Arabs, until it has spread among them that there is a sorcerer in Quraysh and a soothsayer in Quraysh! By Allah, we await nothing but the cry of a pregnant woman, that some of us will rise against others with swords until we destroy one another! O man, if your need is what drives you, we will gather wealth for you until you become the richest man of Quraysh; and if it is marriage that drives you, choose whichever women of Quraysh you wish and we will marry you to ten of them." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Have you finished?" He said: "Yes." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Ha Mim. A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾ until he reached: ﴿But if they turn away, say, "I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud."﴾ 'Utbah said: "Enough! Enough! Do you have anything other than this?" He said: "No." So he returned to Quraysh, and they said: "What is behind you?" He said: "I have left nothing that I think you would speak to him about except that I have spoken to him." They said: "Did he answer you?" [He said: "Yes." They said: "What did he say?"] He said: "No, by the One who raised it as a sign, I did not understand anything of what he said, except that he warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud." They said: "Woe to you! A man speaks to you in Arabic and you do not know what he said?!" He said: "No, by Allah, I understood nothing of what he said except the mention of the thunderbolt."

Likewise, al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili related it in his Musnad from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah with its chain, the same. [Al-Muntakhab of 'Abd ibn Humayd, no. (1121), and Musnad Abi Ya'la (3/349); in its chain is al-Ajlah al-Kindi, whom al-Nasa'i and others declared weak.]

Al-Baghawi also cited it in his Tafsir with his chain from Muhammad ibn Fudayl, from al-Ajlah — and he is Ibn 'Abd Allah al-Kindi [al-Kufi] — who was somewhat weakened, from al-Dhayyal ibn Harmalah, from Jabir, and he mentioned the hadith up to His saying: ﴿But if they turn away, say, "I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud."﴾ Then 'Utbah put his hand over his mouth, begged him by the ties of kinship, and returned to his family without going out to Quraysh, and he delayed from them. Abu Jahl said: "O assembly of Quraysh, by Allah, we see that 'Utbah has only inclined toward Muhammad and was pleased with his food, and that is only because of a need that has befallen him. Come, let us go to him." They went to him, and Abu Jahl said: "O 'Utbah, what has kept you from us except that you have inclined toward Muhammad and his food pleased you? If you have a need, we will gather for you from our wealth what will make you independent of Muhammad's food." 'Utbah became angry and swore that he would never speak to Muhammad again, and said: "By Allah, you know that I am among the wealthiest of Quraysh, but I went to him, related the matter to him, and he answered me with something which, by Allah, is neither poetry, nor soothsaying, nor magic. He recited the surah until he reached: ﴿But if they turn away, say, 'I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud.'﴾ I put my hand over his mouth and begged him by the ties of kinship to stop, and you know that when Muhammad says something, he does not lie, and I feared that the punishment would descend upon you." [Ma'alim al-Tanzil of al-Baghawi (7/167).]

This narration is more like the account of al-Bazzar and Abu Ya'la, and Allah knows best.

Imam Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar also related this story in the Book of the Biography, in a different pattern from this one, saying: Yazid ibn Ziyad related to me from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: I was told that 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah — and he was a chief — said one day while he was sitting in the assembly of Quraysh, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting alone in the mosque: "O assembly of Quraysh, shall I not go to Muhammad, speak with him, and present to him some matters, perhaps he will accept some of them, and we will give him whichever he wishes, and he will leave us alone?" This was when Hamzah had embraced Islam, and they saw the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ increasing and multiplying. They said: "Yes, O Abu al-Walid, go to him and speak with him." 'Utbah rose and went until he sat down beside the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O son of my brother, you know your standing among us in lineage and rank in the tribe, and you have brought your people a great matter: you have divided their community, made their dreams foolish, reviled their gods and their religion, and declared unbelievers those of their forefathers who passed away. So listen to me, I will present to you matters, consider them, perhaps you will accept some of them from us." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Speak, O Abu al-Walid, I am listening." He said: "O son of my brother, if you seek by what you have brought wealth, we will gather for you from our wealth until you become the richest of us. If you seek honour, we will make you our lord, so that we decide no matter without you. If you seek kingship, we will make you king over us. And if what comes to you is a spirit (ra'i) that you see and cannot repel from yourself, we will seek a physician for you and spend our wealth on him until we cure you of it, for a companion (jinn) often overcomes a man until he is treated for it" — or as he said to him. When 'Utbah had finished, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had been listening to him, he said: "Have you finished, O Abu al-Walid?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then listen to me." He said: "I will do so." He said: ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Ha Mim. A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. A Book whose verses have been detailed, an Arabic Qur'an for a people who know, a bringer of good tidings and a warner, but most of them turn away, so they do not hear﴾. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ continued reciting it to him. When 'Utbah heard it, he listened attentively, leaned back with his hands behind him, supporting himself on them, listening to him. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reached the prostration in it, prostrated, and said: "You have heard, O Abu al-Walid, what you have heard, so the matter is yours." 'Utbah rose to his companions, and some of them said to others: "I swear by Allah, Abu al-Walid has come to you with a face other than the one he went with." When he sat with them, they said: "What is behind you, O Abu al-Walid?" He said: "Behind me is that I have heard a speech, by Allah, the like of which I have never heard. By Allah, it is neither magic, nor poetry, nor soothsaying. O assembly of Quraysh, obey me and leave the matter to me: leave the man between himself and what he is in, and withdraw from him, for by Allah, his word that I heard will have a great outcome. If the Arabs overcome him, you will have been spared him by others; and if he prevails over the Arabs, his kingdom will be your kingdom, his honour your honour, and you will be the happiest of people through him." They said: "By Allah, he has bewitched you, O Abu al-Walid, with his tongue!" He said: "This is my opinion about him, so do whatever you see fit." [See Sirat Ibn Hisham (1/293).]

This narration is more like the previous one, and Allah knows best.

Tafsir of Surah Fussilat

It is a Meccan surah.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

* *

His saying: ﴿A Book whose verses have been detailed﴾ means: its meanings have been made clear and its rulings have been firmly established. ﴿An Arabic Qur'an﴾ means: it is in an Arabic language, clear and evident. Its meanings are distinguished and its words are plain, not obscure. That is: it is miraculous in both its wording and its meaning. ﴿Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or behind it. It is a revelation from One who is All-Wise and Praiseworthy﴾ [Fussilat: 42].

* *

His saying: ﴿for a people who know﴾ means: only the firmly grounded scholars recognize this clarity and explicitness. ﴿As a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾ means: at times it gives good tidings to the believers, and at times it warns the disbelievers. ﴿But most of them turn away, so they do not hear﴾ means: most of the Quraysh, so they do not understand anything from it despite its clarity and explicitness.

Allah the Exalted says: "Say," O Muhammad, to these deniers, the polytheists: "I am only a human being like you. It is revealed to me that your God is only One God" (not as you worship, from idols, rivals, and scattered lords). Indeed, Allah is the One God. "So take a straight course toward Him," i.e., devote worship sincerely to Him in the manner He commanded you through the tongues of the Messengers. "And seek His forgiveness," i.e., for the sins of the past. "And woe to the polytheists," i.e., destruction for them and ruin upon them.

"Who do not give zakah." Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas: it means those who do not testify that there is no god but Allah. Ikrimah also said the same.

This is like His saying: "He has succeeded who purifies it, and he has failed who corrupts it" (Ash-Shams: 9–10), and His saying: "He has succeeded who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord and prays" (Al-A'la: 14–15), and His saying: "Then say, 'Would you like to purify yourself?'" (An-Nazi'at: 18). Here, zakah means the purification of the soul from vile characteristics, and the most important part of that is purifying the soul from shirk. The zakah of wealth is so named because it purifies wealth from what is unlawful, and it becomes a cause of its increase, blessing, and abundant benefit, and a means of enabling it to be used in acts of obedience.

As-Suddi said: "And woe to the polytheists who do not give zakah," i.e., they do not hold zakah as a religious obligation.

Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah said: "They are not among the people of zakah."

Qatadah said: "They withhold the zakah of their wealth."

This is the apparent meaning according to many commentators, and Ibn Jarir chose it. However, there is a problem with it: the obligation of zakah was instituted in the second year after the Hijrah (migration) to Madinah, as mentioned by more than one scholar, whereas this verse is Meccan. Unless it is said that it is not unlikely that the origin of zakah, which is charity, was commanded at the beginning of the prophethood, as in His saying: "And give its due on the day of its harvest" (Al-An'am: 141). As for zakah with its nisab (minimum threshold) and fixed amounts, its rulings were clarified in Madinah. This would reconcile the two views, just as the origin of prayer was obligatory before sunrise and before sunset at the beginning of the prophethood. Then, on the night of the Isra' (Night Journey), a year and a half before the Hijrah, Allah enjoined the five daily prayers upon His Messenger (ﷺ), and afterward He detailed its conditions, pillars, and related matters little by little. And Allah knows best.

Then He said after that: "Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have a reward that will never end" (Fussilat: 8). Mujahid and others said: it is neither cut off nor reduced. This is like His saying: "Abiding therein forever" (Al-Kahf: 3), and His saying: "a gift not cut off" (Hud: 108).

As-Suddi said: "ghayr mamnun" means "not reproached" or "not counted as a favor upon them." Some of the Imams rejected this interpretation, since favor (minnah) belongs to Allah upon the people of Paradise. Allah the Exalted said: "Rather, Allah confers favor upon you that He has guided you to faith" (Al-Hujurat: 17), and the people of Paradise said: "So Allah conferred favor upon us and protected us from the punishment of the scorching wind" (At-Tur: 27). And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Except that Allah covers me with His mercy and His bounty."

It is revealed to me that your God is only One God" (not as you worship, from idols, rivals, and scattered lords). Indeed, Allah is the One God. "So take a straight course toward Him," i.e., devote worship sincerely to Him in the manner He commanded you through the tongues of the Messengers. "And seek His forgiveness," i.e., for the sins of the past. "And woe to the polytheists," i.e., destruction for them and ruin upon them.

"Who do not give zakah." Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas: it means those who do not testify that there is no god but Allah. Ikrimah also said the same.

This is like His saying: "He has succeeded who purifies it, and he has failed who corrupts it" (Ash-Shams: 9–10), and His saying: "He has succeeded who purifies himself, and remembers the name of his Lord and prays" (Al-A'la: 14–15), and His saying: "Then say, 'Would you like to purify yourself?'" (An-Nazi'at: 18). Here, zakah means the purification of the soul from vile characteristics, and the most important part of that is purifying the soul from shirk. The zakah of wealth is so named because it purifies wealth from what is unlawful, and it becomes a cause of its increase, blessing, and abundant benefit, and a means of enabling it to be used in acts of obedience.

As-Suddi said: "And woe to the polytheists who do not give zakah," i.e., they do not hold zakah as a religious obligation.

Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah said: "They are not among the people of zakah."

Qatadah said: "They withhold the zakah of their wealth."

This is the apparent meaning according to many commentators, and Ibn Jarir chose it. However, there is a problem with it: the obligation of zakah was instituted in the second year after the Hijrah (migration) to Madinah, as mentioned by more than one scholar, whereas this verse is Meccan. Unless it is said that it is not unlikely that the origin of zakah, which is charity, was commanded at the beginning of the prophethood, as in His saying: "And give its due on the day of its harvest" (Al-An'am: 141). As for zakah with its nisab (minimum threshold) and fixed amounts, its rulings were clarified in Madinah. This would reconcile the two views, just as the origin of prayer was obligatory before sunrise and before sunset at the beginning of the prophethood. Then, on the night of the Isra' (Night Journey), a year and a half before the Hijrah, Allah enjoined the five daily prayers upon His Messenger (ﷺ), and afterward He detailed its conditions, pillars, and related matters little by little. And Allah knows best.

Then He said after that: "Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have a reward that will never end" (Fussilat: 8). Mujahid and others said: it is neither cut off nor reduced. This is like His saying: "Abiding therein forever" (Al-Kahf: 3), and His saying: "a gift not cut off" (Hud: 108).

This passage gives a detailed explanation of His saying: ﴿He created the heavens and the earth in six days﴾ [al-A'raf: 54]. Here He details what is specific to the earth from what is specific to the heaven. He mentioned that He created the earth first, because it is like the foundation, and the principle is that one begins with the foundation and then with the roof, as He said: ﴿It is He who created for you all that is on earth; then He turned to the heaven and made them seven heavens﴾ [al-Baqarah: 29], to the end of the verse.

As for His saying: ﴿Are you more difficult to create, or is the heaven? He constructed it, raised its height and made it proportionate, and darkened its night and brought forth its morning. In this verse, the spreading of the earth (dahw) was after the creation of the heaven. The dahw is explained by His saying: ﴿He brought forth from it its water and its pasture﴾, and this was after the creation of the heaven. As for the creation of the earth itself, it was before the creation of the heaven, by the explicit text. Ibn 'Abbas answered in this way, as reported by al-Bukhari (ﷺ-related collection) in his Sahih when commenting on this verse, for he said:

Al-Minhal reported from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: A man said to Ibn 'Abbas: "I find in the Qur'an things that contradict one another for me." He said: "[Such as] ﴿So there will be no kinship between them that Day, nor will they ask one another﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 101]; ﴿And they will approach one another, questioning each other﴾ [al-Saffat: 27]; ﴿And they will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾ [al-Nisa': 42]; ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 23]. So did they conceal in this verse?" And [the man mentioned] ﴿Or is the heaven? He constructed it…﴾ until His saying: ﴿and spread it out﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 27–30], where He mentioned the creation of the heaven before the earth. Then He said: ﴿Say: "Do you indeed disbelieve in the One who created the earth in two days…"﴾ until His saying: ﴿willingly or unwillingly﴾ [Fussilat: 11], where He mentioned the creation of the earth before the heaven? And He said: ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Nisa': 96], ﴿Exalted in Might and Wise﴾ [al-Nisa': 56], ﴿Hearing and Seeing﴾ [al-Nisa': 58]. It is as if He was and then passed on." 

He [Ibn 'Abbas] said: "So there will be no kinship between them that Day, nor will they ask one another" refers to the first blast. Then the trumpet will be blown: ﴿And the one who is in the heavens and the one who is on the earth will fall dead, except whom Allah wills﴾ [al-Zumar: 68]. So there will be no kinship between them at that time, nor will they ask one another. Then at the second blast: ﴿And they will approach one another, questioning each other.﴾

As for His saying: ﴿We were not polytheists﴾ and ﴿They will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾, Allah forgives the sins of the people of sincerity. The polytheists will say: "Come, let us say, 'We were not polytheists.'" Then their mouths will be sealed and their hands will speak. At that moment they will know that Allah does not conceal any statement. And at that time ﴿Those who disbelieved will wish﴾ [al-Hijr: 2], and so on.

Then He spread out the earth; its spreading is that He brought forth from it water and pasture, and He created the mountains, the stones, the hills and what is between them in two other days. That is His saying: ﴿spread it out﴾, and His saying: ﴿created the earth in two days﴾. So the earth and what is in it were created in four days, and the heavens were created in two days.

﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Nisa': 96]: He named Himself by that, and that is His saying, that is, He has always been so, for Allah does not will anything except that it reaches what He wills. So let the Qur'an not appear contradictory to you, for all of it is from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Al-Bukhari said: Yusuf ibn 'Adi related it to me, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Amr, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah, from al-Minhal, who is Ibn 'Amr, with the hadith.

So His saying: ﴿created the earth in two days﴾ means the day of Sunday and the day of Monday.

﴿And He placed firm mountains on it from above it and blessed it﴾, that is, He made it blessed, receptive to goodness, to sowing and to planting. ﴿And He determined therein its sustenance﴾, which is what its people need of provisions and the places where crops and plants are grown. This refers to Tuesday and Wednesday; these, along with the two previous days, make four. For this reason He said: ﴿in four days, equal for those who ask﴾, that is, for whoever wishes to ask about it in order to know it.

Mujahid and 'Ikrimah said regarding His saying: ﴿And He determined therein its sustenance﴾: He placed in every land what is not suitable in others, such as the 'asab (striped cloth) in Yemen, the sabiri (a type of cloth) in Sabur, and the tayalisah (shawls) in Rayy.

Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah and al-Suddi said regarding His saying: ﴿equal for those who ask﴾, that is, for whoever wishes to ask about it.

Ibn Zayd said: Its meaning is: ﴿And He determined therein its sustenance in four days, equal for those who ask﴾, that is, in accordance with the desire of the one who has a need for provision or a need [of any kind], for Allah has determined for him what he needs.

This statement resembles what they mention regarding His saying: ﴿And He gave you of all that you asked of Him﴾ [Ibrahim: 34]. And Allah knows best.

As for His saying: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke﴾, that is, vapour of water rising from it when the earth was created. ﴿He said to it and to the earth: "Come willingly or unwillingly."﴾ That is: respond to My command and be affected by My action, obediently or unwillingly.

Al-Thawri reported from Ibn Jurayj, from Sulayman ibn Musa, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying ﴿He said to it and to the earth: "Come willingly or unwillingly."﴾ He said: Allah, Exalted, said to the heavens: "Rise up with My sun, My moon and My stars." And He said to the earth: "Split open your rivers and bring forth your fruits." So they both said: ﴿We come willingly.﴾

Ibn Jarir chose this view, may Allah have mercy on him.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: If they had refused His command, He would have punished them with a punishment that they would feel. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

﴿So He completed them as seven heavens in two days﴾, that is, He finished arranging them as seven heavens in two days, namely the Thursday and the Friday.

﴿That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾, that is, the Almighty who has overcome everything, subdued it and conquered it; the All-Knowing of all the movements and stillnesses of the creatures.

He said: "Allah created the earth on Sunday and Monday, and He created the mountains on Tuesday and what is in them of benefits, and on Wednesday He created the trees, the water, the cities, the population and the ruins. These are four." [This is] "Say: 'Do you indeed disbelieve in the One who created the earth in two days and set up rivals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds. And He placed firm mountains on it from above it and blessed it and determined therein its sustenance in four days, equal for those who ask.'" For whoever asks. He said: "And on Thursday He created the heaven, and on Friday He created the stars, the sun, the moon, the angels, until three hours remained of it. In the first of these three hours He created the appointed terms, when whoever dies dies; in the second He cast the calamity upon everything from which people benefit; and in the third [He created] Adam, and settled him in Paradise, commanded Iblis to prostrate to him, and expelled him from it in the last hour." Then the Jews said: "Then what, O Muhammad?" He said: "Then He established Himself upon the Throne." They said: "You have been right, if only you had completed it!" They said: "Then He rested." The Prophet ﷺ became extremely angry, and [the verse] was revealed: ﴿And We created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and no fatigue touched Us. So be patient over what they say﴾ [Qaf: 38].

At that moment they will know that Allah does not conceal any statement. And at that time ﴿Those who disbelieved will wish﴾ [al-Hijr: 2], and so on.

That is His saying: ﴿spread it out﴾, and His saying: ﴿created the earth in two days﴾. So the earth and what is in it were created in four days, and the heavens were created in two days.

﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Nisa': 96]: He named Himself by that, and that is His saying, that is, He has always been so, for Allah does not will anything except that it reaches what He wills. Says Allah, the Exalted: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who deny the truth you have brought them: "If you turn away from what I have brought you from Allah, then I warn you of the descent of Allah's punishment upon you, just as it descended upon the earlier nations who denied the messengers: ﴿a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of ʿAd and Thamud﴾," meaning: and whoever is similar to them, from among those who did the same as they did.

﴿When the messengers came to them from before them and from behind them﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 21], like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And mention the brother of ʿAd, when he warned his people in al-Ahqaf, and warners had already passed before him and after him﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 21], meaning: in the towns neighbouring their lands, Allah sent to them messengers commanding them to worship Allah alone, with no partner, as bringers of good news and as warners. They saw what Allah had brought down upon His enemies of punishments, and what He had clothed His friends with of blessings, yet despite this they did not believe nor did they affirm, but rather they denied and rejected, and said: ﴿If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down angels﴾, meaning: if Allah had sent messengers, they would have been angels from Him. ﴿Indeed, we disbelieve in what you have been sent with﴾, meaning: O humans, ﴿we disbelieve﴾, meaning: we will not follow you, while you are humans like us.

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿As for ʿAd, they were arrogant in the earth [without right]﴾ [the bracketed words are supplied from manuscripts], meaning: they transgressed, rebelled and disobeyed. ﴿And they said: "Who is mightier than us in strength?"﴾, meaning: they boasted of the strength of their build and their power, and believed that by it they could protect themselves from the might of Allah! ﴿Did they not see that Allah, who created them, is mightier than them in strength?﴾, meaning: do they not reflect upon the One against whom they wage enmity? He is the Mighty who created things and placed in them the powers that sustain them, and His seizing is severe, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿And the heaven We built with might, and indeed We are its expanders﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 47]. So they waged enmity against the Compeller, denied His signs and disobeyed His messenger. For this reason He said: ﴿So We sent upon them a furious wind﴾. Some of them said: it is the one that blows with great intensity. It was also said: the cold one. It was also said: the one that has a sound.

The truth is that it had all of these qualities: it was a strong, powerful wind, so that their punishment would be of the same kind as what they had been deceived by, namely their strength; and it was cold, extremely severe in its coldness, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿With a furious, violent wind﴾ [al-Haqqah: 6], meaning: cold and severe; and it had a disturbing sound. From this the famous river in the lands of the East was named "Sarsar," for the strength of the sound of its flow.

His saying: ﴿on days of ill omen﴾, meaning: consecutive, ﴿seven nights and eight days, continuously﴾ [al-Haqqah: 7], like His saying: ﴿on a day of continuous ill omen﴾ [al-Qamar: 19], meaning: the punishment began for them on a day of ill omen for them, and this ill omen continued upon them for seven nights and eight days until it annihilated them to the last one, and the disgrace of this world was joined to them with the punishment of the Hereafter. * *

His saying: ﴿Until, when they reach it﴾, meaning they stand before it, ﴿their hearing, their sight and their skins will testify against them concerning what they used to do﴾ [[In T: "yaksibun" (they earn), which is an error.]], meaning concerning their deeds, both what they put forward and what they left behind. Not a single letter of it will be concealed.

﴿And they will say to their skins: "Why did you testify against us?"﴾, meaning they will blame their limbs and skins when they testify against them. At that point the limbs answer them: ﴿They will say: "Allah has given us speech, the One who gives speech to everything, and He created you the first time, and to Him you will be returned."﴾, meaning He cannot be opposed or prevented, and to Him you are returned.

The Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim narrated to us, Ali ibn Qadim narrated to us, Sharik narrated to us, from Ubayd al-Muktib, from al-Sha'bi [[In T: "And al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar narrated it with his chain."]], from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed one day and smiled, and said: "Will you not ask me what I laughed at?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, at what did you laugh?" He said: "I marvelled at the servant's disputing with his Lord on the Day of Resurrection. He says: 'My Lord, did You not promise me that You would not wrong me?' He says: 'Yes.' He says: 'Then I do not accept any witness against me except from myself.' Allah, blessed and exalted, says: 'Is it not enough that I am a witness against you, and the noble recording angels?' He said: 'Then he repeats these words many times.'" He said: "Then his mouth will be sealed, and his limbs will speak of what he used to do. He will say: 'Away with you, perish! It was for your sake that I was disputing.'"

Then he (al-Bazzar) and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Abu Amir al-Asadi, from al-Thawri, from Ubayd al-Muktib, from Fudayl ibn Amr, from al-Sha'bi, then he said: "We do not know of anyone who narrated it from Anas except al-Sha'bi." It was also recorded by Muslim and al-Nasa'i together, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Nadr, from Abu al-Nadr, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Ash'ari [[Text: al-Ash'ja'i]], from al-Thawri with this chain [[Sahih Muslim, no. 2969, and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 11653.]]. Then al-Nasa'i said: "I do not know anyone who narrated it from al-Thawri except al-Ash'ja'i." And it is not as he said, as you have seen, and Allah knows best.

His saying: ﴿And you did not hide yourselves lest your hearing or your sight or your skins should testify against you﴾, meaning: the limbs and skins will say to them, when they blame them for testifying against them: "You did not hide from us what you were doing; rather you openly defied Allah with disbelief and sins, and you did not care about Him, in your opinion, because you did not believe that He knew all your actions." For this He said: ﴿But you thought that Allah does not know much of what you do. That was your opinion which you held about your Lord; it has destroyed you﴾, meaning this corrupt assumption, which is your belief that Allah does not know much of what you do, is what has ruined and destroyed you before your Lord. ﴿So you became among the losers﴾, meaning in the stations of the Resurrection you lost yourselves and your families.

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Umarah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid [[In T: "Imam Ahmad narrated it with his chain."]], from Abd Allah, who said: "I was hiding behind the curtains of the Ka'bah when three men came: a Qurashi, and his two in-laws from Thaqif, or a Thaqafi and his two in-laws from Quraysh, with much fat on their bellies and little understanding in their hearts. Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 41, verse 19–24 (part 2 of 2):

His saying: ﴿So if they endure, the Fire is their dwelling place; and if they ask to be granted favour, they will not be among those granted favour.﴾ That is: it makes no difference to them whether they endure or do not endure; they are in the Fire, with no escape from it and no exit from it for them. Ibn Jarir said: The meaning of His saying ﴿and if they ask to be granted favour﴾ is: they ask to be returned to the world, but there is no response for them. He said: This is like His saying, reporting about them: ﴿They will say, "Our Lord, our wretchedness overcame us, and we were a misguided people. Our Lord, bring us out of it; then if we return [to disbelief], indeed we will be wrongdoers." He will say, "Remain in it, and do not speak to Me."﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 106–108].

Allah, the Exalted, mentions that He is the One who misguided the polytheists, and that this happened by His will, His decree and His power, and He is Wise in His actions. This came through the companions He appointed for them from the devils of mankind and the jinn: ﴿So they made attractive to them what was before them and what was behind them﴾. That is, they made their deeds appear good to them in the past, and regarding the future they saw themselves only as doers of good. As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he is to him a companion. And indeed, they (the devils) avert them from the way, while they think that they are guided﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 36-37].

* *

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And the word has come into effect against them﴾, that is, the word of punishment, just as it came into effect against the nations who passed away before them, of those who did as they did, from among the jinn and mankind: ﴿Indeed, they were losers﴾, that is, they and those like them were equal in loss and destruction.

* *

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Do not listen to this Quran, and make noise during it"﴾. That is, they urged one another not to obey the Quran or submit to its commands. ﴿And make noise during it﴾, that is, when it is recited, do not listen to it. As Mujahid said regarding ﴿and make noise during it﴾, meaning: with *al-mukaa'* (whistling) and *al-tasdiyah* (clapping), and confusing speech, when the Quran was recited to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the Quraysh did this.

Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and make noise during it﴾, "Criticize it."

Qatadah said: "Deny it, reject it, and oppose it."

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 41, verses 30–32 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast﴾ meaning: they made their deeds sincerely for Allah, and they acted in obedience to Allah the Exalted according to what Allah prescribed for them.

The Hafiz (memoriser and scholar of hadith) Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: al-Jarrah narrated to us, Salm [in A: "Muslim"] ibn Qutaybah Abu Qutaybah al-Sha'iri narrated to us, Suhayl [in A: "Sahl"] ibn Abi Hazm narrated to us, Thabit narrated to us [in T: "Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili narrated with his chain"], from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited to us this verse: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast﴾ and said: "Some people have said it, and then most of them disbelieved [in A: "then they disbelieved"]. Whoever says it until he dies, then he is among those who have remained steadfast upon it."

Likewise, al-Nasa'i narrated it in his Tafsir, and al-Bazzar and Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari), from Amr ibn Ali al-Fallas, from Salm [in A: "Muslim"] ibn Qutaybah, with the same chain [Musnad Abi Ya'la 6/213; al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. 11470; Tafsir al-Tabari 24/73]. Likewise, Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from his father, from al-Fallas, with the same chain. Then Ibn Jarir said:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Amir ibn Sa'd [in A: "Sa'id"], from Sa'id [in T: "Ibn Jarir narrated it from Sa'id"] ibn Nimran [in A: "Mihran"], who said: I recited this verse in the presence of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast﴾. He said: "They are those who did not associate anything with Allah."

Then it was narrated from the hadith of al-Aswad ibn Hilal, who said: Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "What do you say about this verse: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast﴾?" They said: "[They are those who remain steadfast] from sin." He said: "You have taken it to a meaning other than its proper meaning. [The verse means]: ﴿Those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast﴾, so they did not turn to any other god besides Him."

Likewise said Mujahid, Ikrimah, al-Suddi, and others [in T: "Mujahid and others"].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Abd Allah al-Zahrani [in A: "al-Tabarani"] narrated to us, Hafs ibn Umar al-Adani informed us, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from Ikrimah, who said: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, was asked: "Which verse in the Book of Allah is the easiest [to bear]?" He said: His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast﴾ [in T: "Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated with his chain from Ibn Abbas that he was asked"], upon the testimony that there is no god but Allah.

Al-Zuhri said: Umar recited this verse on the pulpit, then said: "By Allah, they remained steadfast for Allah in obedience to Him, and they did not dodge [their obligations] like the dodging of foxes."

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast﴾ means: upon performing His obligations. Likewise said Qatadah, who added: "al-Hasan used to say: 'O Allah, You are our Lord, so grant us steadfastness.'"

Abu al-Aliyah said: ﴿Then remain steadfast﴾ means: they made their deeds and their religion sincerely for Him.

Imam Ahmad said: Hushaym narrated to us, Ya'la ibn Ata narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn Sufyan al-Thaqafi, from his father [in T: "Imam Ahmad narrated with his chain"], that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, instruct me about a matter in Islam about which I will not ask anyone after you." He said: "Say, 'I believed in Allah,' then be steadfast." I said: "What should I guard against most?" He pointed to his tongue.

al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Shu'bah, from Ya'la ibn Ata, with the same [Musnad 4/384; al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. 11489].

Then Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd informed us, Ibn Shihab narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Ma'iz al-Ghamidi, from Sufyan [in T: "Ahmad narrated from Sufyan"] ibn Abd Allah al-Thaqafi, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, tell me about a matter that I may hold fast to." He said: "Say, 'My Lord is Allah,' then be steadfast." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you fear most for me?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took hold of the tip of his own tongue, then said: "This."

Likewise, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it [in A: "like this, and like that"] from the hadith of al-Zuhri, with the same [Musnad 3/413; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2410; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 3972]. al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih."

Muslim in his Sahih and al-Nasa'i also narrated it from the hadith of Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Sufyan ibn Abd Allah al-Thaqafi, who said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, tell me a statement in Islam about which I will not ask anyone after you.' He said: 'Say, "I believed in Allah," then be steadfast.'" and he mentioned the rest of the hadith [Sahih Muslim no. 38].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿The angels descend upon them﴾, Mujahid, al-Suddi, Zayd ibn Aslam, and his son said: this means at the time of death, saying: ﴿Do not fear﴾. Mujahid, Ikrimah, and Zayd ibn Aslam said: meaning, do not fear what you are about to face of the matters of the Hereafter, ﴿and do not grieve﴾ over what you have left behind of the matters of this world, of children, family, wealth, or debt, for We will be your successors regarding them. ﴿And rejoice in the Paradise that you were promised﴾: so they give them good news of the departure of evil and the attainment of good.

This is like the hadith of al-Bara' [may Allah be pleased with him] [Note: the hadith of al-Bara' was previously cited at the commentary on verse 40 of Surah al-A'raf, but this wording is the wording of the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, and it is recorded in the same place]: "The angels say to the soul of the believer: 'Come out, O good soul, from the good body which you used to inhabit. Come out to rest and sweet scents, and to a Lord who is not angry.'"

It was also said: the angels descend upon them on the day they come out of their graves. This was related by Ibn Jarir from Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Abd al-Salam ibn Mutahhar narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated to us: I heard Thabit recite Surah Ha Mim al-Sajdah [in T: "Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Thabit that he recited al-Sajdah"] until he reached: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast, the angels descend upon them﴾, then he paused and said: "We have been told that when Allah raises the believing servant from his grave, the two angels who were with him in the world meet him and say to him: 'Do not fear and do not grieve, and rejoice in the Paradise that you were promised.'" [in T, S, A: "And rejoice" – which is an error.] He said: "Then Allah secures his fear and gladdens his eye. No dreadful matter that people fear on the Day of Resurrection will be but a delight to the eye of the believer, because of what Allah guided him to and because of what he used to do for Him in the world."

Zayd ibn Aslam said: "They give him good news at his death, in his grave, and when he is resurrected." Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

This view encompasses all the other views, and it is very good, and it is the correct one.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿We are your allies in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾, meaning: the angels say to the believers at the time of dying: "We were your allies, i.e., your companions, in the life of this world. We guided you, granted you success, and protected you by the command of Allah. Likewise, we will be with you in the Hereafter, easing your loneliness in the graves and at the blowing of the Trumpet, granting you security on the Day of Resurrection, bringing you across the Straight Path, and bringing you to the Gardens of Bliss." ﴿And for you therein is whatever your souls desire﴾: meaning, in Paradise there is everything you choose that souls desire and eyes delight in. ﴿And for you therein is whatever you ask for﴾: meaning, whatever you request, you will find it, and it will be present before you as you have chosen. ﴿As a welcome from the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful﴾: meaning, as hospitality, bounty, and favour from the Most Forgiving of your sins, the Most Merciful to you, the Most Kind, Who has forgiven, concealed, shown mercy, and been gentle.

Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned here the hadith of the "Marketplace of Paradise" at His saying: ﴿And for you therein is whatever your souls desire, and for you therein is whatever you ask for, as a welcome from the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful﴾. He said:

My father narrated to us, Hisham ibn Ammar narrated to us, Abd al-Hamid ibn Habib ibn Abi al-Ashirin Abu Sa'id narrated to us, al-Awza'i narrated to us, Hassan ibn Atiyyah narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, that he met Abu Hurayrah [may Allah be pleased with him], and Abu Hurayrah said: "We ask Allah to gather me and you in the marketplace of Paradise." Sa'id said: "Is there a marketplace in it?" He said: "Yes. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ informed me that when the people of Paradise enter it, they will descend according to the merit of their deeds. Then they will be permitted, for a period equal to a Friday of worldly days, to visit Allah, Mighty and Majestic. His Throne will be displayed to them, and He will manifest Himself to them in a garden of the gardens of Paradise. Pulpits of light will be placed for them, and pulpits of pearls, pulpits of ruby, pulpits of emerald, pulpits of gold, and pulpits of silver. The least of them will sit [in A: 'upon them'], and there is no one lowly among them, upon dunes of musk and camphor. They will not see that the people of the chairs have a more excellent sitting than them."

Abu Hurayrah said: "I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, shall we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection?'" He said: "Yes. Do you doubt seeing the sun and the moon on a full-moon night?" We said: "No." He ﷺ said: "Likewise, you will not doubt seeing your Lord, the Exalted. No one in that gathering will remain without Allah addressing him directly, to the extent that He will say to one of them: 'O so-and-so, son of so-and-so, do you remember the day you did such and such?'—reminding him of some of his lapses in the world—and he will say: 'O Lord, did You not forgive me?' He will say: 'Yes; by the vastness of My forgiveness you have reached this station of yours.'" He said: "While they are in that state, a cloud will overshadow them from above and rain down upon them a fragrance the like of which they have never smelled before."

He said: "Then our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, will say: 'Arise to what I have prepared for you of honour, and take what you desire.'" He said: "So we will come to a marketplace surrounded by angels, containing what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no heart has conceived. He said: 'Whatever we desire will be carried to us, and nothing in it is sold or bought.' In that marketplace the people of Paradise meet one another." He said: "The man of high rank will approach and meet one lower than himself—and there is no lowly person among them—and he will be startled by the clothing he sees on him, and before the end of his speech, he will be presented with something better than it. This is because it is not befitting for anyone to grieve in it."

"Then we return to our homes, and our wives will greet us, saying: 'Welcome and well come, our beloved! You have come with beauty and fragrance greater than what you had when you left us.' He will say: 'We sat today with our Lord, the Almighty, Mighty and Majestic, and it is our right to return with the like of what we have returned with.'"

al-Tirmidhi narrated it in "The Description of Paradise" in his Jami', from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Hisham ibn Ammar; and Ibn Majah narrated it from Hisham ibn Ammar, with the same in substance [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2549; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 4336]. Then al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a gharib hadith; we do not know it except through this route."

And Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him, and whoever dislikes to meet Allah, Allah dislikes to meet him." We said [[In A: "qala" (he said).]]: "O Messenger of Allah, do we all dislike death?" He said: "That is not the dislike of death. Rather, when the believer is at the point of death, there comes to him the good news from Allah of what he is going to, so nothing is more beloved to him than to have met Allah, and Allah loves to meet him." He said: "And when the wicked person (or the disbeliever) [is at the point of death], there comes to him what he is going to of evil, or what he will suffer of evil, so he dislikes meeting Allah, and Allah dislikes to meet him." [[In A: "uhtudir" (was at the point of death).]]

This is a sound hadith [[Al-Musnad (3/107).]], and it has been reported in the Sahih from another route [[Reported by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (6507), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2683), by way of Qatadah, from Anas, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, with a similar wording to the hadith mentioned above.]].

Allah says: **"And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah"** — that is, calls the servants of Allah to Him — **"and does righteous deeds and says, 'Indeed, I am of the Muslims'"** — that is, while he himself is guided by what he says. So his benefit is both to himself and to others, and it is necessary and transitive. He is not among those who enjoin righteousness while not doing it themselves, and forbid wrongdoing while committing it. Rather, he enjoins good and abandons evil, and calls the creation to the Creator, blessed and exalted is He. This applies generally to everyone who calls to good while being guided in himself. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is the most worthy of people of this, as Muhammad ibn Sirin, as-Suddi, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said.

It has also been said that what is meant by it is the righteous muezzins (callers to prayer), as is established in Sahih Muslim: "The muezzins will have the longest necks of people on the Day of Resurrection" [Sahih Muslim, no. 387, from Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan, may Allah be pleased with him]. And in the Sunan, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "The imam is responsible, and the muezzin is trusted; so may Allah guide the imams and forgive the muezzins" [Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (2/232), Abu Dawud in his Sunan (no. 8/5), and at-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (no. 207)].

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: Ali ibn al-Husayn told us, Muhammad ibn Arwa al-Harawi told us, Ghassan the judge of Herat told us. And Abu Zur'a said: Ibrahim ibn Tahman told us, from Matar, from al-Hasan, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas that he said: "The arrows of the muezzins before Allah on the Day of Resurrection are like the arrows of the mujahidin, and he, between the adhan and the iqamah, is like one writhing in his blood in the way of Allah."

He said: Ibn Mas'ud said: "If I were a muezzin, I would not mind not performing Hajj, Umrah, or jihad."

He said: Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "If I were a muezzin, my affair would be complete, and I would not mind not standing in night prayer or fasting by day. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say, 'O Allah, forgive the muezzins,' three times." He said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, you have left us, and we are fighting one another with swords over the adhan." He said: "No, O Umar. There will come upon people a time when they will abandon the adhan because of their weakness, and those are flesh which Allah has forbidden to the Fire — the flesh of the muezzins."

[Narrated by al-Isma'ili in his Musnad, as in Musnad Umar by Ibn Kathir (1/144), through Ibrahim ibn Tahman from Matar from al-Hasan al-Basri from Umar; al-Hasan did not hear from Umar.]

He said: A'isha said, and this verse is for them: **"And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah and does righteous deeds and says, 'Indeed, I am of the Muslims'"**. She said: it is the muezzin when he says, "Hasten to prayer," for he has called to Allah.

Likewise Ibn Umar and Ikrimah said: it was revealed concerning the muezzins.

Al-Baghawi mentioned from Abu Umama al-Bahili, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said, regarding **"and does righteous deeds"**: "It means praying two rak'ahs between the adhan and the iqamah."

Then al-Baghawi cited the hadith of Abdullah ibn al-Mughaffal, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Between every two calls (adhan and iqamah) there is a prayer." Then he said for the third time: "For whoever wishes." It has been recorded by the compilers in their books from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Buraydah, from him [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 627; Sahih Muslim no. 838; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 2283; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 185; Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/28); Sunan Ibn Majah no. 1162]; and the hadith of al-Thawri, from Zayd al-Ammi, from Abu Iyas Mu'awiya ibn Qurra, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: al-Thawri said: "I do not think it except that he raised it to the Prophet (ﷺ): 'Supplication is not rejected between the adhan and the iqamah.'"

Abu Dawud, at-Tirmidhi, and an-Nasa'i in "al-Yawm wal-Laylah" all narrated it from the hadith of al-Thawri with this wording [Sunan Abi Dawud no. 521; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 212; an-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. 9896]. At-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan hadith."

An-Nasa'i also narrated it from the hadith of Sulayman at-Taymi, from Qatadah, from Anas, with this wording [an-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. 9899].

The correct view is that the verse is general, applying to the muezzins and to others. As for the circumstances of its revelation, the adhan had not been legislated at all, for the surah is Meccan, and the adhan was legislated only in Madinah after the Hijrah, when Abdullah ibn Zayd ibn Abd Rabbih al-Ansari was shown it in a dream, and he related it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who commanded him to give it to Bilal, for he had the more resonant voice, as is established in its proper place. So the correct view is that it is general, as Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan al-Basri, that he recited this verse, **"And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah and does righteous deeds and says, 'Indeed, I am of the Muslims'"**, and said: "This is the beloved of Allah, this is the friend of Allah, this is the elect of Allah, this is the chosen one of Allah, this is the most beloved of the people of the earth to Allah. He answered Allah in his call, and he called the people to what Allah had answered in his call, and he did righteous deeds in answering Him, and he said, 'Indeed, I am of the Muslims.' This is the successor (khalifah) of Allah."

* *

His saying: **"And good and evil are not equal."** That is, there is a great difference between this and that. **"Repel [evil] with that which is better."** That is, whoever wrongs you, repel him from yourself by doing good to him, as Umar [may Allah be pleased with him] said: "You do not punish one who disobeys Allah concerning you with anything like obeying Allah concerning him."

* *

His saying: **"And thereupon the one between whom and you there is enmity [will become] as though he were a devoted friend."** The "devoted friend" (hamim) is the close friend. That is: if you do good to one who wronged you, that good will lead him to reconciliation with you, to affection for you, and to compassion toward you, until he becomes as though he were a close devoted friend to you, that is, near to you in sympathy for you and kindness to you.

Then He said: **"But none is granted it except those who are patient."** That is: none accepts this counsel and acts upon it except one who is patient in that, for it is hard on the souls. **"And none is granted it except one of great fortune."** That is: one who has a abundant share of happiness in this world and the Hereafter.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the interpretation of this verse: Allah commanded the believers to be patient at anger, forbearing at ignorance, and forgiving at injury. When they do that, Allah protects them from Satan, and their enemy submits to them as though he were a devoted friend.

* *

His saying: **"And if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in Allah."** That is: the devil of mankind may be deceived by kindness done to him, but as for the devil of the jinn, there is no remedy against him when he whispers except seeking refuge in his Creator, who empowered him over you. When you seek refuge in Allah and take shelter in Him, He restrains him from you and turns back his plot. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say when he stood for prayer: "I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan, from his pricking, his blowing, and his spitting" [see the takhrij of this hadith under the commentary on verse 97 of Surah al-Mu'minun].

We have already mentioned that this context has no parallel in the Qur'an except in Surah al-A'raf, at His saying: **"Take what is forgiving, enjoin what is good, and turn away from the ignorant. And if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is Hearing and Knowing"** [al-A'raf: 199–200], and in Surah al-Mu'minun, at His saying: **"Repel evil with that which is better; We are most knowing of what they describe. And say, 'My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the suggestions of the devils. And I seek refuge in You, my Lord, lest they be present with me'"** [al-Mu'minun: 96–98].

[But what is mentioned in al-A'raf is lighter on the soul than what is mentioned in Surah Fussilat, because turning away from the ignorant and leaving him is lighter on the soul than doing good to the one who does evil; the soul takes pleasure in that, and it needs no effort except through treatment, and Satan assists it in this state, so it yields to him and disobeys its owner, and so it needs struggle and strength of faith. For this reason it is emphasized here with the pronoun of separation and the definite article, when He says: **"So seek refuge in Allah; indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing."**]

Then he said for the third time: "For whoever wishes." He answered Allah in his call, and he called the people to what Allah had answered in his call, and he did righteous deeds in answering Him, and he said, 'Indeed, I am of the Muslims.' This is the successor (khalifah) of Allah."

* *

His saying: **"And good and evil are not equal."** That is, there is a great difference between this and that. **"Repel [evil] with that which is better."** That is, whoever wrongs you, repel him from yourself by doing good to him, as Umar [may Allah be pleased with him] said: "You do not punish one who disobeys Allah concerning you with anything like obeying Allah concerning him."

* *

His saying: **"And thereupon the one between whom and you there is enmity [will become] as though he were a devoted friend."** The "devoted friend" (hamim) is the close friend. That is: if you do good to one who wronged you, that good will lead him to reconciliation with you, to affection for you, and to compassion toward you, until he becomes as though he were a close devoted friend to you, that is, near to you in sympathy for you and kindness to you.

Then He said: **"But none is granted it except those who are patient."** That is: none accepts this counsel and acts upon it except one who is patient in that, for it is hard on the souls. **"And none is granted it except one of great fortune."** That is: one who has a abundant share of happiness in this world and the Hereafter.

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the interpretation of this verse: Allah commanded the believers to be patient at anger, forbearing at ignorance, and forgiving at injury. When they do that, Allah protects them from Satan, and their enemy submits to them as though he were a devoted friend.

* *

When you seek refuge in Allah and take shelter in Him, He restrains him from you and turns back his plot. So his benefit is both to himself and to others, and it is necessary and transitive. He is not among those who enjoin righteousness while not doing it themselves, and forbid wrongdoing while committing it. Rather, he enjoins good and abandons evil, and calls the creation to the Creator, blessed and exalted is He. This applies generally to everyone who calls to good while being guided in himself. He said: Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "If I were a muezzin, my affair would be complete, and I would not mind not standing in night prayer or fasting by day. **The commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 41, verses 40–43:**

His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who deviate concerning Our signs﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: *al-ilhad* (deviation, distortion of the truth) is placing speech in other than its proper places.

Qatadah and others said: it is disbelief and obstinacy.

* *

His saying: ﴿They are not hidden from Us﴾. That is, it is a severe threat and a firm warning, meaning that He, the Exalted, knows those who deviate concerning His signs, His names, and His attributes, and He will requite them with punishment and retribution. Therefore He said: ﴿Is he who is cast into the Fire better, or he who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection?﴾ That is, are these two equal? They are not equal.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said, threatening the disbelievers: ﴿Do what you will.﴾ Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and 'Ata' al-Khurasani said: ﴿Do what you will﴾ is a warning, meaning whether good or evil. "Indeed, He is Knowing of you and Seeing of your deeds." Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do.﴾

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it came to them﴾. al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, and Qatadah said: it is the Quran. ﴿And indeed, it is a Mighty Book﴾, that is, it is protected from being approached; no one can hope to bring the like of it.

﴿Falsehood cannot come at it from before it or from behind it﴾. That is, there is no way for falsehood to reach it, because it is sent down from the Lord of the worlds. Therefore He said: ﴿A revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy.﴾ That is, All-Wise in His sayings and His deeds; *Hamid* in the sense of *mahmud* (praised), meaning that in all that He commands and forbids, its consequences and ends are praiseworthy.

Then He said: ﴿Nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you.﴾ Qatadah, al-Suddi, and others said: what is said to you of denial is only like what was said to the messengers before you. Just as you were denied, they were denied; and just as they endured the harm of their peoples toward them, so you endure the harm of your people toward you. This is the view preferred by Ibn Jarir, and neither he nor Ibn Abi Hatim related any other view.

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Possessor of forgiveness [for mankind]﴾ [an addition from manuscript A]. That is, for whoever repents to Him. ﴿And Possessor of painful punishment﴾, that is, for whoever persists in his disbelief, his transgression, his obstinacy, his opposition, and his defiance.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd [in manuscript T: "Ibn Abi Hatim related from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab"], from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Possessor of forgiveness﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Were it not for Allah's forgiveness and His pardoning, no one would have enjoyed life; and were it not for His threat and His punishment, everyone would have become complacent." [Its chain is mursal, and 'Ali ibn Zayd is agreed upon to be weak.]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 41, verse 44–45:

When Allah, the Exalted, mentioned the Qur'an, its eloquence and its rhetorical power, and its perfection in both its wording and its meaning, and yet the polytheists did not believe in it, He drew attention to the fact that their disbelief in it was the disbelief of obstinacy and wilful opposition, as He said: ﴿And if We had sent it down upon some of the non-Arabs, and he had recited it to them, they would not have believed in it﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 198, 199]. Likewise, even if the entire Qur'an had been revealed in the language of the non-Arabs, they would have said, out of wilful obstinacy and opposition: ﴿Why are its verses not explained in detail? What, a non-Arabic (recitation) and an Arab (messenger)?﴾. That is, they would have said: "Why was it not revealed in detail in the language of the Arabs?" and they would have denied it, saying: "Non-Arabic and Arabic?" That is: how could a non-Arabic speech be revealed to an Arab addressee who does not understand it?

This meaning has been narrated in this way from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Suddi, and others.

It has also been said: the meaning of their words ﴿Why are its verses not explained in detail? What, a non-Arabic (recitation) and an Arab (messenger)?﴾ is: "Why was not some of it revealed in the non-Arabic language and some of it in the Arabic?"

This is the view of al-Hasan al-Basri, who used to recite it thus, without the interrogative in his saying ﴿a non-Arabic﴾. It is also a narration from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and it is more emphatic in obstinacy and opposition.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: It is, for those who believe, a guidance and a healing﴾. That is: say, O Muhammad: this Qur'an, for those who believe in it, is guidance for their hearts and a healing for what is in the breasts of doubts and uncertainty. ﴿And as for those who do not believe, there is deafness in their ears﴾, that is, they do not understand what is in it; ﴿and it is for them a blindness﴾, that is, they are not guided to the clarity it contains, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers, but it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss﴾ [al-Isra: 82].

﴿Those are called from a far place﴾. Mujahid said: that is, far from their hearts.

Ibn Jarir said: its meaning is: as if the one addressing them is calling them from a far place, so they do not understand what he says [Tafsir al-Tabari (24/81)].

I say: this is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿The likeness of those who disbelieve is like that of one who shouts to that which hears nothing but calls and cries — deaf, dumb, blind; so they do not reason﴾ [al-Baqarah: 171].

Al-Dahhak said: they will be called on the Day of Resurrection by their most hideous names.

Al-Suddi said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) was sitting with a man from among the Muslims who was judging between people, when suddenly he said: "Labbayka!" ['Here I am!']. 'Umar said: "Why do you answer? Did you see anyone, or did anyone call you?" He said: "A caller called me from beyond the sea." 'Umar said: "Those are called from a far place." Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We had certainly given Musa the Scripture, but it was disputed over﴾, that is, he was denied and harmed. ﴿So be patient, as the messengers of determination were patient﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 35]. ﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord [decreeing] a specified term﴾ [al-Shura: 14], meaning the postponement of the reckoning until the Day of Return, ﴿the matter would have been judged between them﴾, that is, He would have hastened the punishment for them. Rather, they have an appointment from which they will not find any refuge besides Him. ﴿And indeed they are, concerning it, in disquieting doubt﴾. That is: their denial of it was not from insight regarding what they said; rather, they were doubtful about what they said, not certain of anything they held. This is how Ibn Jarir interpreted it, and it is possible, and Allah knows best.

﴿And if We let him taste mercy from Us after some adversity has touched him, he will surely say, "This is my due."﴾ Meaning: when good and provision reach him after he was in hardship, he will surely say, "This is my due; I deserved it from my Lord." ﴿And I do not think the Hour will ever come﴾, meaning he disbelieves in the establishment of the Hour, because he has been granted a blessing, so he boasts, becomes arrogant, and disbelieves, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿No! Indeed, man transgresses, because he sees himself self-sufficient﴾ [Al-'Alaq: 6-7].

﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, indeed I shall have with Him the best [reward]﴾, meaning: even if there is a return, my Lord will surely treat me well, as He treated me well in this world. He wishes upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, despite his evil deeds and lack of certainty. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then We will surely inform those who disbelieved of what they did, and We will surely make them taste a severe punishment﴾. Allah the Exalted threatens whoever has this deed and belief with punishment and retribution.

Then He says: ﴿And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and distances himself [with his] side﴾, meaning he turns away from obedience and is arrogant toward submitting to the commands of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as in His saying: ﴿So he turned away with his power﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 39].

﴿And when evil touches him﴾, meaning hardship, ﴿then he is one of extensive supplication﴾, meaning he prolongs asking about one matter. Wordy speech (al-kalam al-'arid) is that whose wording is long and whose meaning is little, and the concise (al-wajiz) is its opposite, which is that whose meaning is little yet indicative. Allah the Exalted has also said: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side or sitting or standing; but when We remove his harm from him, he passes on as if he had never called Us to a harm that touched him﴾ [Yunus: 12].

Allah says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who deny the Qur'an: ﴿Have you considered: if this Qur'an is from Allah, and you disbelieve in it,﴾ meaning: how do you see your state in the sight of the One who sent it down to His Messenger? For this reason He said: ﴿Who is more astray than one who is in extreme dissension?﴾ meaning: in disbelief, obstinacy, and opposition to the truth, and on a path far from guidance.

Then He said: ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves﴾ meaning: We will make manifest to them Our proofs and evidences that the Qur'an is the truth, sent down from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to His Messenger ﷺ, by external signs ﴿in the horizons﴾: from the conquests and the manifestation of Islam over the regions and all other religions.

Mujahid, al-Hasan and al-Suddi said: "And signs within themselves" refers to the Battle of Badr, the Conquest of Makkah, and similar events that befell them, in which Allah granted victory to Muhammad and his companions and humbled falsehood and its party.

It is also possible that what is meant is what a human being is composed of, what is within him and upon him of substances, humours and wondrous forms, as is explained in the science of anatomy, which points to the wisdom of the Creator, blessed and exalted. Likewise, what he is naturally disposed to of divergent characters, of good, of bad, and what is between these, and what he is subject to under decrees which he cannot pass by his own power, strength, or stratagem, and his caution against transgressing or exceeding them, as Ibn Abi al-Dunya recited in his book "al-Tafakkur wa'l-I'tibar", from his teacher Abu Ja'far al-Qurashi:

When you look, seeking a lesson, then look at yourself, for in you there is a lesson.

You are the one who morning and evening lives in this world, and all its affairs are admonitions.

You are the one who was turned about in youth, then greatness took hold of your person.

You are the one whose creation proclaims his death; hair and skin proclaim it from him.

You are the one who is given and then deprived; caution does not save him from being deprived.

You are the one to whom nothing of himself belongs, and destiny is more entitled to his wealth.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth. Is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is over all things a witness?﴾ meaning: Allah suffices as a witness over the deeds and words of His servants, and He testifies that Muhammad is truthful in what he reports from Him, as He said: ﴿But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you; He sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness﴾ [An-Nisa: 166].

* *

His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, they are in doubt about the meeting with their Lord﴾ meaning: they are in doubt about the establishment of the Hour. For this reason they do not reflect upon it, nor do they act for it, nor do they beware of it; rather it is to them something worthless that they do not heed, though it is a certain reality, with no doubt about it, and an event that is inevitable.

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim related to us, Khalaf ibn Tamim related to us, Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Ansari related to us: that Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz ascended the pulpit, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: "Amma ba'd. O people, I did not gather you for a matter I am introducing among you, but I reflected on this matter to which you are returning, and I knew that the one who believes in it is a fool, and the one who denies it is ruined." Then he descended.

As for the meaning of his saying, may Allah be pleased with him, "that the one who believes in it is a fool": that is, because he does not work for it the work fitting it, nor does he beware of it, nor fear its terror, while he is nonetheless affirming it and certain of its occurrence, yet he continues in his play, heedlessness, desires and sins. He is therefore a fool in this respect, and "fool" (ahmaq) in the language means one weak in intellect.

* *

His saying: "and the one who denies it is ruined." This is clear, and Allah knows best.

Then Allah, exalted is He, said, affirming that He is over all things Powerful, encompassing all things, and that the establishment of the Hour is easy and simple for Him, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿Unquestionably, He encompasses all things﴾ meaning: all created beings are under His subjugation and in His grasp, within the folds of His knowledge, and He is the One who disposes of all of them by His judgment: whatever He wills comes to be, and whatever He does not will does not come to be. [End of the commentary on Surah Fussilat]
